workPackages.title: HTTP tracker client, BEP 12 announcer and announce loop
workPackages.notes: Implement internal/bt/tracker/contract.go: delete stub.go and provide newHTTPClient, newAnnouncer, startLoop, Event.String and (*FailureError).Error. Depends only on merged code (internal/bt/bencode for lenient decoding via bencode.Unmarshal, internal/clock). Read ADR-0014. All tests in contract_test.go must pass with -race: TestContractEventString, TestContractAnnounceQuery, TestContractAnnounceResponse, TestContractAnnounceErrors, TestContractAnnouncerTiers, TestContractAnnouncerShuffle, TestContractLoopLifecycle, TestContractLoopRetry, TestContractLoopCompletedBeforeStarted, TestContractLoopStopBounded. Pitfalls: (1) percent-encode info_hash and peer_id byte by byte as %XX for every byte outside [A-Za-z0-9.-_~]; never use url.Values.Encode for them (it emits '+' for spaces) and keep any query already in the announce URL. (2) compact=1 and numwant=50 on EVERY announce, including stopped; event omitted for EventNone. (3) Decode responses with lenient bencode into a struct or map; 'peers' may be a byte string (compact, 6 bytes/peer) or a list of dicts (ip/port/peer id); drop port 0 and non-IP hostnames; also read compact 'peers6' (18 bytes/peer). complete/incomplete absent -> -1. (4) The Loop must use cfg.Clock (never time.Now/After/Sleep/NewTimer: the T1 lint forbids them in internal/bt/**) and hold at most one clock timer at a time, only while idle; the tests poll clock.Fake.Waiters() to know the loop is idle. Completed() must wake an idle loop immediately (use a channel, not the timer). (5) Stop(ctx) cancels the loop's internal context (aborting an in-flight HTTP request), waits for the goroutine, then sends one stopped announce bounded by ctx, and returns its error; idempotent. (6) Announcer: shuffle each tier once at construction (rnd may be nil = no shuffle), try tiers in order, promote the successful URL to the front of its tier, remember tracker id per URL; all failing -> errors.Join of the individual errors. No UDP (M5): a udp:// URL is just a failing tracker. Coverage >= 80%. Add your own unit tests (e.g. a URL encoder table test, malformed responses).

workPackages.title: Peer wire protocol and connection
workPackages.notes: Implement internal/bt/peer/contract.go: delete stub.go and provide writeHandshake, readHandshake, exchangeHandshake, readMessage, writeMessage, newConn and newPeerID. Depends only on merged code (internal/clock). All tests in contract_test.go must pass with -race (handshake bytes, peer id, message round trip and wire format, size limits, invalid messages, 20k garbage inputs, ExchangeHandshake incl. ctx cancel, Conn delivery/send order/close semantics, protocol violations, remote close -> io.EOF, Close from OnMessage, keep-alive and idle timeout with clock.Fake, send queue limit). Pitfalls: (1) Check the 4-byte length prefix BEFORE allocating: length > MaxMessageLen is ErrMessageTooLarge unless the id byte is bitfield (5), whose payload may be up to maxBitfieldLen (<= 0 or > MaxBitfieldLen means MaxBitfieldLen). Read the id byte first, then decide; never read the payload of an oversize message (the test reader fails if you do). (2) Exact payload sizes: choke/unchoke/interested/not-interested 0, have 4, request/cancel 12, piece >= 8, port 2, otherwise ErrInvalidMessage; unknown ids within the limit are returned with Payload (not an error). Zero length = keep-alive (Message{KeepAlive:true}). (3) Never panic on any input. (4) Conn: one read goroutine calling cfg.OnMessage sequentially (keep-alives not delivered), one write goroutine draining a queue; Send never blocks; > SendQueueLimit queued -> close with ErrSendQueueFull. Close is idempotent, non-blocking and safe from inside OnMessage; Done is closed after both goroutines exit and nc is closed; Err() is nil if Close came first, wraps io.EOF on remote close, else the protocol error; OnClose(err) called exactly once after Done. (5) Timers: use cfg.Clock only (T1 lint: no time.Now/After/Sleep/NewTimer/NewTicker in internal/bt/**), create every timer before newConn returns; keep-alive after KeepAliveInterval without writes; ErrIdleTimeout after IdleTimeout without reads, and push the idle deadline back BEFORE calling OnMessage. Do not use net.Conn read deadlines computed from the clock for idle detection (a fake clock's time is not wall time); to unblock reads on close, close nc. (6) exchangeHandshake: write ours, read theirs, compare info-hash; abort promptly when ctx is done (e.g. a goroutine that closes nc or sets an immediate deadline on ctx.Done, or SetDeadline(ctx.Deadline())), and leave no goroutine behind. (7) newPeerID: '-TD0100-' + 12 bytes from rnd, deterministic for a given source. No BEP 6/10 at M3; reserved bytes are zero. Coverage >= 80%. Consider adding a FuzzDecodeMessage target in your own peer_test.go (WIRE-06 arrives at M4).

workPackages.title: Bitfield and piece picker
workPackages.notes: Implement internal/bt/piece/contract.go: delete stub.go and provide newPicker, pipelineDepth, Layout.PieceSize, Layout.NumBlocks and the Bitfield methods (NewBitfield, FromBytes, Len, Has, Set, Clear, Count, Full, Bytes, Clone) on the frozen struct `Bitfield{n int; bits []byte}`. Pure in-memory logic, no goroutines, no I/O, no time; depends on nothing. Read ADR-0012. All tests in contract_test.go must pass. Rules that the black-box gate depends on: (1) Pick order: pieces already in progress (a block outstanding or received) first by lowest index, then new pieces rarest-first (availability = number of registered peers having the piece) with ties by LOWEST INDEX. No random-first, no endgame at M3: a block outstanding for any peer is never handed out again. STOR-02 fails if a single-peer download is not sequential. (2) Blocks are 16 KiB aligned; only the last block of a piece is shorter; never cross a piece end. (3) Received(p, b) accepts a block only if its geometry matches the layout exactly, its piece is neither verified nor pending, and it was not received before; it does not need to be outstanding for p; an accepted block leaves every peer's outstanding set. pieceDone is reported exactly once per completion; the piece is then pending (not picked) until PieceVerified or PieceFailed (which makes all its blocks needed again). (4) Release(p) returns p's outstanding blocks but keeps its availability; RemovePeer also forgets availability. (5) Bitfield: wire order (piece 0 = high bit of byte 0); FromBytes rejects wrong lengths and set spare bits with ErrInvalidBitfield; out-of-range Has/Set/Clear never panic. (6) PipelineDepth = clamp(rate*2/16384, 5, 250). Keep Pick efficient: a 4 MiB torrent with 256 KiB pieces and 250 outstanding requests must not be quadratic in the number of blocks per call; track per-piece state rather than scanning every block of the torrent. Coverage >= 80%.

workPackages.title: Piece-to-file storage, .part files, SHA-1 verification
workPackages.notes: Implement internal/bt/storage/contract.go: delete stub.go and provide open(dir, info, opts) (Storage, error). Depends only on merged code (internal/bt/metainfo for Info/File). Read ADR-0013. All tests in contract_test.go must pass with -race (spanning files + .part renames + zero-length file, corruption detection, BEP 47 pad files never on disk and read as zeros, unsafe paths and relative dir rejected, range errors and ErrClosed, existing .part data kept and extended, at most MaxOpenFiles descriptors under concurrent use of 300 files). Pitfalls: (1) metainfo.File.Path already includes the torrent name for multi-file torrents; the on-disk path is filepath.Join(dir, Path...). Validate EVERY path with filepath.IsLocal(filepath.Join(Path...)) before creating anything (ErrUnsafePath). (2) Open: MkdirAll(dir); for each non-pad file, create parents, then create <path>.part with Truncate(Length) (sparse, no data written) unless <path> or <path>.part already exists (never truncate or delete existing data; extend a shorter .part). Zero-length files are created as <path> directly. Pad files: never create, open or rename; reads of pad ranges return zeros, writes to them are dropped. Preallocation must close each file (respect MaxOpenFiles). (3) A piece and a block may span many files; map [pieceOffset+begin, +len) onto files by Offset/Length (binary search). (4) MarkVerified: a file is complete when every piece overlapping [Offset, Offset+Length) is verified; then close its cached handle and rename <path>.part -> <path>; later reads must use the new name. Idempotent. (5) Concurrency: the Storage is called from many goroutines at once; bound concurrent disk ops with a semaphore of DiskWorkers (default 4) and concurrent VerifyPiece calls with HashWorkers (default max(1, GOMAXPROCS/2)); the handle LRU must never close a handle another goroutine is using (reference count) and must keep open handles <= MaxOpenFiles (default 128) at every instant. (6) WantedBytes(i) = bytes of piece i that fall in non-pad files (this is what completedBytes grows by). No time or randomness needed; no goroutines that outlive a call. Coverage >= 80%.

integration.notes: Read ADR-0011..0015 and the contract.go files of every package. Order: (1) merge the four work packages; run go test -race ./internal/bt/... (contract tests of tracker, peer, piece, storage must pass). (2) internal/bt/session: delete stub.go, implement newSession per session/contract.go and ADR-0015 until session/contract_test.go passes with -race. Session: bind TCP ':<PeerPort>' (0 = any; on failure keep going, ListenErr reports it); accept and close incoming conns; peer ID via peer.NewPeerID(cfg.Rand), tracker key random hex per process; Add: duplicate check first (ErrAlreadyExists), then absolute DownloadDir + MkdirAll (ErrInvalidDownloadDir), register, publish Status, start actor. Actor: checking = storage.Open (sparse .part) -> downloading: tracker.StartLoop(Announcer over m.Trackers grouped by Tier; Stats from atomics: Left = SizeBytes - CompletedBytes) and dial OnPeers addresses (<= 50 peers, <= 20 concurrent dials, 10 s timeout, skip duplicates and our own listen address); per peer: peer.ExchangeHandshake then peer.NewConn with MaxBitfieldLen = ceil(numPieces/8) and OnMessage sending events to the actor channel (select with ctx.Done). Event handling: bitfield -> piece.FromBytes (invalid -> disconnect) -> Picker.PeerBitfield, send interested; have -> PeerHave; unchoke -> fill pipeline; choke -> Picker.Release; piece -> Picker.Received (rejected -> WastedTotal += len, never written), DownloadedTotal += len always; accepted -> storage.WriteBlock in a goroutine -> on write done, if pieceDone run storage.VerifyPiece in a goroutine -> ok: MarkVerified, Picker.PieceVerified, CompletedBytes += storage.WantedBytes(i), publish; fail: Picker.PieceFailed, WastedTotal += PieceSize(i). Top up EVERY unchoked peer's pipeline after each received block and after any peer disconnects (blocks released by a dead peer must go to the survivors): want = piece.PipelineDepth(rate) - Outstanding. Disconnect -> Picker.RemovePeer. All verified -> state seeding, CompletedAt, Loop.Completed(), publish (CompletedBytes == SizeBytes in the same snapshot). Close(ctx): stop all actors; Loop.Stop with a ctx bounded by ShutdownAnnounceTimeout, in parallel; close conns, storage, listener; wait for goroutines; Close(ctx) must not leak goroutines (the test counts them). Never call time.Now etc. directly in internal/bt/** (use cfg.Clock); rand from cfg.Rand. Split session into several files (< 800 lines each). (3) internal/api: register the M3 route table exactly as in internal/api/contract.go (the method-less /api/v1/torrents/preview pattern must go: use 'GET /api/v1/torrents/preview' -> 405 and a method-less '/api/v1/torrents/{id}' fallback that answers 405 with Allow POST for id 'preview' and Allow GET otherwise); add handler reusing readTorrentUpload + metainfo.Parse; map session.Status to api.Torrent; make api/contract_test.go and the existing api tests pass. (4) cmd/torrentd: create the session at startup with PeerPort from config (PeerPortUnset -> 0 or the stored listen_port setting), DefaultDownloadDir from the default_download_dir setting if present, clock.Real(), the slog logger; pass it as api.Options.Torrents. On SIGTERM run Session.Close (3 s announce budget) concurrently with the HTTP shutdown, then mark clean shutdown and close the DB (ADR-0015 §3). (5) Black-box gate: harness/factory gate --ms 3 -v, then --upto 3. Docker must be running for SP-01 (libtorrent seeder). Likely trouble spots: TRK-01 stopped within 3.5 s of SIGTERM; WIRE-04 (must connect to >= 20 of 40 garbage peers in 30 s: dial concurrently, short handshake timeout); STOR-06 (lsof counts open files under the download dir: only storage may hold handles); WIRE-02 (oversize peer disconnected while the good peer is stalled).
